h_src:
You route customer support tickets for a software shop.
Labels: spam, legal, priority, billing_dispute, refund_auto, refund_review, bug_critical, bug, account, shipping, feedback.

House rules (apply in this order):
1. Enterprise plan: any real request or complaint (billing problems such as charges after cancellation, feature requests, issues) is priority, not billing_dispute or feedback. Only spam or legal threats override this. (Enterprise refund requests follow rule 2.)
2. Refund requests (customer simply wants money back, e.g. 'don't need it', 'not what I expected', 'doesn't fit my use case'). Decide using Plan and purchase age:
 - Purchased within 7 days (any order type, any plan) -> refund_auto.
 - Plan Free -> refund_review (when older than 7 days), regardless of order type.
 - Paid plan (Team, Pro, Enterprise, etc.), older than 7 days: physical order purchased within 30 days -> refund_auto; digital order -> refund_review; anything older than 30 days -> refund_review.
 Politeness and wording do not change this.
3. Digital order where delivery shows complete but the download/license/access is missing -> account (never shipping). Shipping is only for physical order delivery problems.
4. For non-Enterprise plans: charged after cancelling or unexpected charges -> billing_dispute; feature requests or suggestions -> feedback; crashes/data loss -> bug_critical; minor defects -> bug; lawsuits/chargeback threats -> legal; junk/promotions -> spam.

Ignore greetings and filler such as 'Quick question', 'Urgent', 'Cheers', 'Please help'. Use the Plan, Order type, and Purchased fields as primary signals.
Reply with exactly one label and nothing else.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: Added inferred house rules: refunds within 30 days for physical orders auto-approve, digital refunds go to review, Enterprise plan tickets about charges or feature requests are priority, and missing digital downloads are account issues.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes refund_auto vs refund_review confusion on physical vs digital orders, Enterprise escalations to priority, and digital delivery problems routed to account instead of shipping.

mem_src.problem: unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: Added inferred house rules: refunds within 14 days for physical orders go to refund_auto, while digital or older refunds go to review; Enterprise plan tickets about charges or feature requests are priority; missing digital downloads are account issues.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes most refund_auto/refund_review mix-ups, the Enterprise priority cases, and the digital-delivery-to-account case, raising accuracy above 75%.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: The failures show the refund rule is driven by purchase recency and plan rather than order type alone: Team digital purchased 2 days ago is refund_auto, while Free physical purchased 14 days ago is refund_review, so I replaced the order-type rule with a short-window rule (within about 7 days -> auto, otherwise review).
mem_src.predicted: Fixes all three observed refund failures (2-day digital -> auto, 14-day physical -> review) while leaving Enterprise priority, account, and other rules unchanged.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: Replaced the order-type-based refund rule with a purchase-recency rule (auto only if purchased within 7 days, any order type; otherwise review), since 14-day physical refunds went to review and a 2-day digital refund went to auto.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes the three refund failures by keying refund_auto on recency (<=7 days) instead of physical/digital, while leaving Enterprise, access, and other rules unchanged.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: Failures show the refund rule is not simply order type: Team digital 2 days -> auto, Free physical 14 days -> review; earlier recency-only rule hurt, so I use a combined rule where auto requires a short window (<=7 days) for any type, while keeping the physical/30-day path only for paid-tier plans, and keep everything else unchanged.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes the three refund failures while limiting regression risk on other refund cases by preserving the physical -> auto default for non-Free plans and digital older purchases -> review.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: Failures show refund routing depends on plan tier and amount, not just order type: Team digital $15 at 2 days is auto, while Free physical at 14 days ($120, $79) is review, so I made refund_auto depend on a low amount or a very recent purchase, with other cases going to review.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes the three observed refund failures (cheap/very recent digital -> auto; Free physical 14-day, $79 and $120 -> review) while leaving Enterprise priority, account, and non-refund rules unchanged.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: The remaining failure is a Free-plan physical order at 14 days that should be refund_auto, so I made the physical-within-30-days path apply to every plan including Free and left Free digital older than 7 days as refund_review.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes the Free physical 14-day refund case (now refund_auto) without changing Free digital, paid-plan, Enterprise, account, or non-refund routing.

mem_src.problem: Unwritten house routing rules (refund window, enterprise priority, digital delivery)
mem_src.rationale: The remaining failure shows a Free-plan physical refund at 14 days is refund_auto, so I changed the Free-plan rule to follow the same physical-within-30-days path as paid plans and left only Free digital refunds older than 7 days in refund_review.
mem_src.predicted: Fixes the Free physical 14-day refund (now refund_auto) while leaving all other refund, Enterprise, account, and non-refund routing unchanged.
